ambiguity_resolutions.n_average: Outcomes average over n in {4,6,8} with nanmean: if some n are missing the mean is over the n present (column n_cov_<outcome> counts them). Seed-mean J first, then rel(), then mean over n.
ambiguity_resolutions.beta: beta = OLS slope of log(seed-mean J of default) on log N over all evaluated N in {2,3,4,6,8,12} with J>0; needs >=3 points, else NaN.
ambiguity_resolutions.nstar: N*(lambda) = argmax over evaluated N in {2,...,12} of Jbar(N) - lambda*N*Jbar(2)/2 (default arm, seed-mean J); NaN if N=2 is missing. Ties -> smallest N.
ambiguity_resolutions.loss_rate: loss rate = seed-mean deaths_per_robot, mean over n in {4,6,8}, of the arm's rows in the chosen score (for 'adv' the row of the minimising adversary).
ambiguity_resolutions.adv_row_columns: For the adversarial score every non-J column (deaths, exposure, speed, tau_stale, ...) comes from the row of the adversary that minimises J for that policy/tempo/n/remove_t.
ambiguity_resolutions.principles: S = tau_act / tau_stale with tau_act = 0.5 / mean(speed) and tau_stale = mean(tau_stale), both means over default-arm rows (seeds x n in {4,6,8}, remove_t=-1) of the chosen score. Means are taken before the ratio.
ambiguity_resolutions.worth: W(t) = (Jfull - Jremoved) * 6 / Jfull with Jfull, Jremoved the seed-mean J of default at n=6 (remove_t=-1 / t). Under the adversarial score both are pool-minimum scores. NaN if Jfull <= 1e-9.
ambiguity_resolutions.per_seed: Per-seed outcomes pair training seed s of every arm with seed s of the other arms; seed spread = std (ddof=1) over seeds per condition. An outcome is 'unresolved' when the pooled seed spread sqrt(mean_c sd_c^2) exceeds the between-condition spread (std over conditions of the seed-mean outcome).
ambiguity_resolutions.transfer_rows: All four models are fitted and scored on the same rows: conditions with finite y, log S, R_late and tempo.
ambiguity_resolutions.transfer_verdict: 'P beats B1 and B2 in held-out MAE by >=10%' means MAE_P <= 0.9*MAE_B1 and MAE_P <= 0.9*MAE_B2. The prereg sentence ends 'on the leave-one-planet-out predictions'; we read that as qualifying both the MAE and the Spearman criterion, so the verdict uses the 36 LOPO predictions. The same criterion on the headline (train single-hazard -> predict combined) split is reported alongside but does not gate.
ambiguity_resolutions.transfer_overall: >=4 of 6 outcomes supported -> 'supported'; 1-3 -> 'partially supported'; 0 -> 'not supported'. Untestable outcomes (NaN metrics) count as not supported and are listed.
ambiguity_resolutions.sign_agreement: Fraction of held-out conditions with sign(pred) == sign(obs) (beta and loss rates are positive, so this metric is trivially ~1 for them).
ambiguity_resolutions.bootstrap: Only per-row mean J and J_sem are available, so uncertainty is propagated parametrically: every eval row's J is redrawn as Normal(J, J_sem) (J_sem NaN -> 0), the pool minimum is re-taken per draw, and the V outcomes are recomputed. This covers evaluation-episode noise only, not seed-to-seed training variation (see seed spread).
ambiguity_resolutions.heuristic_match: 'match or beat the heuristic' = seed-mean J_default >= J_heuristic - 1.645*SE, SE combining the J_sem of both (one-sided 5% non-inferiority). Pass overall if >= 9 of 12 cells pass (cells without data count as fail).
ambiguity_resolutions.adv_drop: Per cell: mean over default rows (all seeds, tempi, n; remove_t=-1) of J_nature - J_adv. 'Most cells' = more than half of the 12 cells show a positive drop.
ambiguity_resolutions.secondary_score: Secondary expectations are evaluated under the same score as the primary test (adversarial) by default; the report also writes the nature-score version as a sensitivity table.
